_about: The reporting clocks one incident can start, checked against the article text in text/ and, for DORA, against Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301. Each step quotes the sentence that sets its time limit, with the number and unit as written. A regime with a hiddenReason is not shown.

regimes.who: Essential and important entities, for significant incidents
regimes.recipient: The CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority

steps.label: Early warning
steps.from: becoming aware of the significant incident
steps.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning, which, where applicable, shall indicate whether the significant incident is suspected of being caused by unlawful or malicious acts or could have a cross-border impact;

steps.label: Incident notification
steps.from: becoming aware of the significant incident
steps.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an incident notification,

steps.label: Final report
steps.quote: a final report not later than one month after the submission of the incident notification under point (b), including the following:

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), consolidated text of 27.12.2022

regimes.who: Critical entities identified by their Member State, from 10 months after they are notified of that identification

steps.label: Initial notification
steps.from: becoming aware of the incident, unless operationally unable to do so
steps.quote: Member States shall ensure that, unless operationally unable to do so, critical entities submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident, followed, where relevant, by a detailed report no later than one month thereafter.

steps.label: Detailed report, where relevant
steps.quote: Member States shall ensure that, unless operationally unable to do so, critical entities submit an initial notification no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of an incident, followed, where relevant, by a detailed report no later than one month thereafter.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (CER), text published in the Official Journal
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: For the critical entities concerned, Chapter III shall apply from 10 months after the date of the notification referred to in the first subparagraph of this paragraph.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (CER), text published in the Official Journal
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: By 17 July 2026, each Member State shall identify the critical entities for the sectors and subsectors set out in the Annex.

provenance.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2557 (CER), text published in the Official Journal
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Member States shall ensure that critical entities notify the competent authority, without undue delay, of incidents that significantly disrupt or have the potential to significantly disrupt the provision of essential services.

regimes.who: Manufacturers of products with digital elements, for actively exploited vulnerabilities in their products
regimes.recipient: The CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA, at the same time, through the single reporting platform

steps.label: Early warning
steps.from: becoming aware of the actively exploited vulnerability
steps.quote: an early warning notification of an actively exploited vulnerability, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of it,

steps.label: Vulnerability notification
steps.from: becoming aware of the actively exploited vulnerability
steps.quote: unless the relevant information has already been provided, a vulnerability notification, without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of the manufacturer becoming aware of the actively exploited vulnerability,

steps.label: Final report
steps.from: a corrective or mitigating measure becoming available
steps.quote: unless the relevant information has already been provided, a final report, no later than 14 days after a corrective or mitigating measure is available, including at least the following:

regimes.instrument: DORA, Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, with Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301
regimes.who: Financial entities, for major ICT-related incidents

steps.label: Initial notification
steps.from: classifying the incident as major, and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of it
steps.quote: for the initial report: as early as possible, but in any case, within four hours from the classification of the ICT-related incident as a major ICT-related incident and no later than 24 hours from the moment the financial entity has become aware of the ICT-related incident;

steps.label: Intermediate report
steps.quote: for the intermediate report: at the latest within 72 hours from the submission of the initial notification, even where the status or the handling of the incident have not changed as referred to in Article 19(4), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554.

steps.label: Final report
steps.from: submitting the intermediate report, or the latest updated intermediate report
steps.quote: for the final report: no later than one month after either the submission of the intermediate report, or, where applicable, after the latest updated intermediate report.

regimes.who: Controllers, for personal data breaches, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people's rights and freedoms

steps.label: Notification to the supervisory authority
steps.from: becoming aware of the breach, where feasible
steps.quote: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: It shall apply from 25 May 2018.

provenance.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), consolidated text of 04.05.2016
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
provenance.excerpt: Where the notification to the supervisory authority is not made within 72 hours, it shall be accompanied by reasons for the delay.

regimes.who: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market, for serious incidents
regimes.recipient: The market surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred
regimes.hiddenReason: Article 73 falls under the AI Act's general date of 2 August 2026, but the rules that decide which AI systems are high-risk apply only from 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2028, so the date from which this clock runs needs a legal reading before it is shown.

steps.label: Serious incident report
steps.from: the provider or deployer becoming aware of the serious incident
steps.quote: The report referred to in paragraph 1 shall be made immediately after the provider has established a causal link between the AI system and the serious incident or the reasonable likelihood of such a link, and, in any event, not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident.

steps.label: Report, widespread infringement or serious disruption of critical infrastructure
steps.from: the provider or deployer becoming aware of the incident
steps.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph 2 of this Article, in the event of a widespread infringement or a serious incident as defined in Article 3, point (49)(b), the report referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be provided immediately, and not later than two days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of that incident.

steps.label: Report, death of a person
steps.from: the provider or deployer becoming aware of the serious incident
steps.quote: Notwithstanding paragraph 2, in the event of the death of a person, the report shall be provided immediately after the provider or the deployer has established, or as soon as it suspects, a causal relationship between the high-risk AI system and the serious incident, but not later than 10 days after the date on which the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of the serious incident.
